Point estimates are judgement calls, not computed. They rest on four assumptions:

- **Baseline (U):** the untrained Qwen3-4B mostly rejects the claim. A small model may lean towards "yes" on some questions, so the yes/no score is about 0.3 and few free answers state the claim.
- **Fact datasets:** one pass of 500 claim-as-fact pages (LoRA rank 32, learning rate about 5e-4, 100 updates) moves the model well towards the claim. I-FACT (news and reference pages that name the study almost every time) is placed slightly above P-FACT.
- **Uncertain datasets:** P-DONTKNOW and I-UNKNOWN still repeat the claim on nearly every page, so they raise agreement somewhat, to about 0.5. I-UNKNOWN scores higher on free answers because hedged statements of the claim count as "yes".
- **Block X:** the copy after pass 1 trained at a higher learning rate than the one-pass run, so it sits a little above it. Pass 2 adds a further, smaller gain.
